_comment: Before this file the p50/p95 existed only as prose in docs, so 'baseline' could
not be compared against by a person or a test, and the only number with teeth
was the overhead ceiling in benchmark/latency.py.
Numbers are seconds per task from the SYNTHETIC stage mode: the stage sleeps a
known 0.050s, so everything above that is platform cost (queue claim, stage
dispatch, artifact rows, logging). Absolute milliseconds are meaningful only
relative to the platform that measured them, which is why reference_platform is
part of the record and why the gate uses a ceiling instead of an expectation.
Only `gated_size` is enforced: image preparation is part of the measured span
and scales with pixels, so a ceiling tuned for 512 px would false-alarm on
4096 px for reasons unrelated to the platform.
and review the diff. tests/unit/test_benchmark_samples.py fails if this file and
the constants in benchmark/latency.py disagree, or if a size disappears.
